answer.rationale: Two live pressures (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) map directly onto the onboarding/signup-simplification line of evidence (memory_31, memory_86), which has shown durable, not just pulled-forward, gains. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the obvious reactive move against the competitor's pricing attack, but the archived record shows it produced pulled-forward revenue and a retention hit rather than sustainable qualified revenue — exactly the failure mode the primary objective warns against, so I verified it to confirm before ruling it out this cycle. I also verified memory_86 rather than memory_31 to check whether the onboarding-completion effect was measured on a comparable segment/timeframe to the current drop, since only one experiment slot exists and the two onboarding-related memories could be reporting overlapping or conflated effects. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives are plausible long-term revenue levers but don't address this quarter's acute activation/onboarding decline, and activation_messaging is a weaker, narrower intervention than fixing the onboarding funnel itself. I'm treating this as a standard experiment rather than broad rollout because even with two supporting memories, the current environment (competitor pricing pressure) is a new confound not present when memory_31/86 were measured, so causal attribution to onboarding changes alone isn't fully certain yet.
